SWF157 (cre-t-157) — Vet-Quote Testimonial Redesign

QA report — petinsurancegurus.com (The Swiftest) — final checks, 2026-09-09

What this test does

Replaces the existing SWF145-era plain-text quote (control) with a redesigned quote card (photo, name/role, source logo, quote-mark), in three flavors:

  • Control — existing SWF145 V1 baseline, plain-text quote, no photo/logo/carousel.
  • V1 — new card design, single quote, no carousel.
  • V2 — new card design, 4-quote carousel, manual pagination only (no autoplay).
  • V3 — new card design, 4-quote carousel, automatic rotation every ~5s (manual pagination still works and still fires the goal; autoplay-triggered transitions do not).

All three variations (and the control) start from the same quote — client-confirmed as “V5 from SWF145”: Dr. Diane Deresienski, Managing Veterinarian, via The New York Times. V2/V3’s carousel adds 3 more (Dr. Rebecca Greenstein, Dr. Katy Nelson, Dr. Karen Halligan — all NYT/NYPost/CBS; GB News correctly excluded).

Result

126 / 128 passed — 2 failed (pre-existing site issue, unrelated to this feature)

Chrome Desktop Safari Desktop Mobile Chrome (Pixel 5) Mobile Safari (iPhone 12)

Resolved: starting-quote question (was an open bug)

An earlier pass flagged the starting quote (Dr. Diane Deresienski / NYT) as possibly wrong against a Figma reference that appeared to show Dr. Sarah Gorman / Small Door Veterinary / CBS News. Client has since confirmed control IS “V5 of SWF145,” and that Diane Deresienski’s quote is the correct one all three variations should start from. Not a defect — the regression checklist above now asserts this directly (TC-11, TC-13, TC-20) instead of flagging it as an open question.

2 failures — pre-existing WebKit-only site issue, unrelated to this feature

Both failures threw the identical error: i.tippy is not a function — the site’s own breed-select tooltip (Tippy.js library) failing to initialize, on WebKit engines only (Safari Desktop and Mobile Safari). This targets #breed-select, a pet-type filter dropdown completely unrelated to the quote card (#comparison-section) this test covers. Did not reproduce on Chrome or Mobile Chrome. Same class of WebKit-specific third-party-script race condition already seen elsewhere on this client’s sites.

Not covered by this test suite

Firefox Desktop, Edge Desktop, and Tablet (iPad Gen 7) were not part of this final-checks pass (scoped to Chrome + Safari, desktop + mobile per this round’s request). Re-run the full 7-project matrix if formal sign-off across all browsers is needed.
